title: New Zealand 119 for two, still 233 behind, after India's record 720 in Wellington
dek: Rishabh Pant's 128 and Dhruv Jurel's 78 took India to the biggest Test total made in New Zealand. Devon Conway's unbeaten 59 kept the hosts going, but India need eight wickets on the last day.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India need eight wickets on the final day to win the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington, after declaring at 720 for nine, the highest total ever made in a Test in New Zealand, and reducing the hosts to 119 for two by stumps on the fourth day on Sunday. New Zealand still trail by 233 runs.

Devon Conway was unbeaten on 59 and Rachin Ravindra on 27 at the close, having added 59 for the third wicket. Jasprit Bumrah had Tom Latham caught behind off the second ball of the innings, leaving the opener with a pair in the match, and Prasidh Krishna removed Henry Nicholls, the first-innings centurion, for 31, caught at short leg by Dhruv Jurel, according to reports.

## India's innings

India had resumed at 486 for four and added 234 runs in two sessions. Rishabh Pant made 128, his ninth Test century, and Jurel 78 off 79 balls. Captain Shubman Gill declared at about 7.13 am IST, when Jurel was stumped off Glenn Phillips, according to reports. New Zealand began their second innings 352 behind, needing to bat for well over a day to save the match.

Pant had resumed on 55 and the nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj yet to score. Kamboj made 38 off 42 balls in a fifth-wicket stand of more than 50 before he was caught off Phillips, according to reports. Pant reached three figures with a six off Phillips shortly after 5 am IST and was out for 128 off 153 balls, with 10 fours and six sixes, caught off Rachin Ravindra just before lunch, which India took at 629 for six.

After the break Jurel reached his fifty and India kept attacking. Akash Deep hit 13 off five balls before he fell, and Jurel's dismissal brought the declaration. Phillips, an occasional off-spinner, took three wickets. The fast bowler Jacob Duffy finished with one for 201 from 33 overs, the second-most expensive figures by a New Zealand bowler in a Test innings, according to reports.

Six Indian batters passed fifty: KL Rahul (136), Pant (128), Gill (98), Yashasvi Jaiswal (85), Devdutt Padikkal (80) and Jurel (78).

## The records

India's total beats the West Indies' 660 for five declared at the same ground in 1995 as the highest by a visiting team in New Zealand, and New Zealand's own 715 for six declared against Bangladesh at Hamilton in 2019 as the highest in any Test in the country, according to reports.

It is India's third-highest Test total, behind 759 for seven declared against England in Chennai in 2016 and 726 for nine declared against Sri Lanka at the Brabourne Stadium in Mumbai in 2009, and their highest outside Asia, ahead of 705 for seven declared at Sydney in 2004, according to reports.

## What happens next

The final day is Monday, 23 November, with play due to start at 3.30 am IST and about 90 overs to be bowled. The second new ball will be due 35 overs into the day, according to reports. New Zealand need another 233 runs just to make India bat again. A win would give India a 1-0 lead in the two-match series and valuable points in the World Test Championship.
